Sibilants (from Latin : sibilans ' hissing ' ) are fricative and affricate consonants of higher amplitude and pitch . [ 1 ] [ page needed ] Examples of sibilants are the consonants at the beginning of the English words s ip , z ip and sh ip . The symbols in the International Phonetic Alphabet used to denote the sibilant sounds in these words are, respectively, [s, z, ʃ, ʒ] . Sibilants have a characteristically intense sound, which accounts for their paralinguistic use in getting one's attention (e.g. calling someone using "psst!" or quieting someone using "shhhh!").
